structure.title: Preface
structure.summary: The text is a formal company letter from Grasim Industries Limited (Ref: GIL/CFD/SEC/26/060/SE, dated 21st July 2025) addressed to BSE and NSE, referencing Regulation 34(1) of SEBI Listing Regulations. It encloses the Integrated Annual Report for FY ended 31st March 2025 and Notice of the 78th AGM to be held on 26th August 2025 via VC/OAVM. The report and notice are sent electronically to registered members and available on the company website. The letter is signed by CFO Pavan Kumar Jain and copied to Luxembourg Stock Exchange and Citi Bank N.A. The included AGM Notice covers ordinary business: adoption of audited standalone and consolidated financial statements, declaration of dividend of Rs. 10 per equity share, and re-appointment of Ms. Ananyashree Birla and Mr. Aryaman Vikram Birla as directors retiring by rotation.

It includes company contact details and outlines four ordinary business items: adoption of audited standalone and consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2025, declaration of a dividend of Rs. 10 per equity share, and re-appointment of two directors retiring by rotation, Ms. Ananyashree Birla and Mr. Aryaman Vikram Birla. Each item is presented with a proposed ordinary resolution.

nodes.title: Sustainability
nodes.summary: The Chairman's Message highlights Grasim Industries' record FY 2024-25 performance with consolidated revenue of ₹1,48,478 crore (US$17 billion), nearly doubled over five years at 15% CAGR, and EBITDA of ₹20,023 crore. Growth was broad-based across Cement, Cellulosic Fibres, Chlorine Derivatives, and Specialty Chemicals. New businesses—Decorative Paints (Birla Opus) and B2B E-commerce (Birla Pivot)—scaled significantly, with Birla Opus targeting ₹10,000 crore revenue in three years and Birla Pivot reaching ₹5,000 crore ARR, aiming for US$1 billion by FY 2026-27. UltraTech's India capacity rose from 140 to 183 million tonnes; Aditya Birla Capital achieved record loan book and AUM; ABRen targets 1 GW annual renewable capacity addition. The message covers sustainability (Net Zero roadmap, ESG governance), capital expenditure exceeding ₹67,000 crore with over ₹51,000 crore growth capex, and strategic expansion in building materials, Lyocell fibres, and specialty chemicals.

Remuneration Policy
The Company’s remuneration policy is directed towards rewarding the performance based on review of achievements. The remuneration policy is in consonance with the existing industry practice. There has been no change in the policy during the year.

Research and Development (R&D)
The R&D projects undertaken by the Company focus on developing and commercialising differentiated premium / new products, improving our competitive cost position, product quality and environmental sustainability. To support these goals, the Company develops a pipeline of projects to address near and mid-term needs, as well as the exploration of future opportunities.

nodes.title: VI. Performance Goal Setting
nodes.summary:
VI. Performance Goal Setting
We aim to ensure that, for both annual incentive plans and long-term incentive plans, the target performance goals shall be achievable and realistic.
Threshold performance (the point at which incentive plans are paid out at their minimum, but non-zero, level) shall reflect a base-line level of performance, reflecting an estimated 90% probability of achievement.
Target per formance is the expected level of performance at the beginning of the performance cycle, taking into account all known relevant facts likely to impact measured performance.
Maximum performance (the point at which the maximum plan pay-out is made) shall be based on an exceptional level of achievement, reflecting no more than an estimated 10% probability of achievement.

The section then details material accounting policies, including business combinations, property, plant and equipment, intangible assets, impairment, inventories, employee benefits, share-based payments, foreign currency, derivatives and hedge accounting, fair value measurement, financial instruments, revenue recognition, leases, borrowing costs, government grants, income tax, provisions, earnings per share, key judgements and estimates, and recent pronouncements, along with supporting schedules for PPE and capital work-in-progress.

nodes.title: A. Basis of Preparation:
nodes.summary: The text provides notes to standalone financial statements for the year ended March 31, 2025. It covers corporate information: Grasim Industries Limited is an Indian public limited company with registered office in Nagda, Madhya Pradesh; its shares are listed on BSE and NSE, and GDRs on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange. The company operates in Cellulosic Fibres, Chemicals, Building Materials, and Others. It also outlines the basis of preparation: financial statements comply with Ind AS, Companies Act 2013, and SEBI guidelines, applied consistently. They are prepared on a going concern basis at historical cost, except for derivative financial instruments, certain financial assets/liabilities, assets held for disposal, employee defined benefit plans, employee stock option plans, and business combination assets/liabilities measured at fair value. Functional and presentation currency is Indian Rupees, rounded to nearest crore up to two decimals.

nodes.title: B. Material Accounting Policies:
nodes.summary: The section covers material accounting policies: business combinations and goodwill; current/non-current classification; property, plant and equipment (deemed cost, component accounting, depreciation, capital work-in-progress); expenditure during construction; intangible assets (including internally generated); discontinued operations and assets held for sale; impairment of non-financial assets; inventories; cash and cash equivalents; cash flow statement; employee benefits (short-term, defined contribution, defined benefit plans including provident fund, gratuity, pension, compensated absences, actuarial valuation, re-measurement in OCI); share-based payments (equity and cash-settled); treasury shares; foreign currency transactions; derivative financial instruments and hedge accounting (cash flow hedges); fair value measurement; financial instruments (initial recognition, classification and measurement of financial assets and liabilities at amortised cost, FVTPL, FVTOCI; impairment using expected credit losses; de-recognition; embedded derivatives; offsetting); revenue recognition (including contract liabilities, variable consideration, financing component, dividend and interest income, claims); leases (lessee accounting, right-of-use assets and lease liabilities, exemptions, sale and leaseback); borrowing costs; trade receivables; government grants; exceptional items; income tax (current and deferred); provisions and contingencies; warranty provisions; earnings per share; key accounting judgements and estimates (lease classification, litigation, impairment of investments, useful lives, defined benefit obligations, fair value measurement, share-based payments, cash dividend); and recent accounting pronouncements (Ind AS 117). It also includes detailed PPE gross block, depreciation, and capital work-in-progress schedules.

nodes.title: B. Material Accounting Policies: (intro)
nodes.summary: This text outlines material accounting policies covering: business combinations and goodwill/capital reserve (acquisition method, control assessment, goodwill measurement, contingent consideration, non-controlling interests, transaction costs); classification of assets/liabilities as current/non-current (12-month operating cycle); property, plant and equipment (deemed cost on Ind AS transition, cost model, component accounting, recognition, derecognition, capital work-in-progress); treatment of expenditure during construction; depreciation (straight-line except Viscose Staple Fibre and Corporate Finance on WDV, useful lives per Schedule II or technical assessment, residual values, pro-rata depreciation, review of estimates); intangible assets (deemed cost, initial measurement, amortization over useful lives, indefinite life assessment); internally generated intangible assets (research expensed, development capitalized if criteria met); discontinued operations and non-current assets held for sale (measurement at lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell); impairment of non-financial assets (annual review, recoverable amount, reversal); inventories (lower of cost and net realizable value, cost formulas); cash and cash equivalents (definition); cash flow statement (indirect method); and employee benefits (short-term, defined contribution, defined benefit plans including provident fund trust, gratuity, pension, actuarial valuation, re-measurement in OCI).

nodes.title: Accounting Policies: Inventories, Cash, Cash Flows, Employee Benefits
nodes.summary: The page outlines accounting policies for inventories, cash and cash equivalents, cash flow statements, and employee benefits. Inventories are valued at the lower of cost or net realisable value, with cost based on weighted-average, including acquisition and conversion costs; obsolete or slow-moving items are provided for, and waste/scrap is valued at net realisable value. Cash and cash equivalents include cash on hand, bank balances, and short-term highly liquid investments with original maturities of three months or less. The cash flow statement uses the indirect method, segregating operating, investing, and financing activities. Employee benefits distinguish short-term benefits (expensed on accrual) and defined contribution plans (provident fund and superannuation contributions expensed when employees render service).

nodes.title: Defined Benefit Plans:
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for employee benefits and related items: defined benefit plans (gratuity, pension, post-employment medical) using actuarial valuation and projected unit credit method, with gratuity funded via trust; provident fund contributions to a company-administered trust with statutory interest and shortfall liability; re-measurement of defined benefit plans recognized in Other Comprehensive Income and retained earnings, not reclassified to profit or loss; defined benefit cost components (service cost, net interest, re-measurement) with first two in profit or loss; discount rate based on government bond yields; balance sheet recognition of deficit or surplus limited to available economic benefits. Compensated absences for earned and sick leave actuarially valued, treated as current, with actuarial gains/losses in profit or loss. Employee share-based payments: equity-settled transactions measured at fair value using Black-Scholes and Binomial models, expensed over vesting period, with forfeiture/lapse adjustments; cash-settled transactions measured at fair value using Black-Scholes Merton Formula, expensed with liability re-measured at each reporting date. Treasury shares via Employee Benefit Trust treated as extension, recognized at cost and deducted from other equity, with no gain/loss on purchase, sale, issue, or cancellation, and share options settled from treasury shares. Foreign currency transactions: initial recognition at transaction date rates, monetary assets/liabilities retranslated at period-end rates, non-monetary items at historical rates.

nodes.title: Employee Benefits, Share-Based Payments, Treasury Shares, and Foreign Currency Notes
nodes.summary: The page covers accounting policies for defined benefit costs, including re-measurement in OCI, cost components, and liability calculation using government bond yields. Compensated absences for earned and sick leave are actuarially valued and presented as current. Employee share-based payments are expensed over the vesting period, with forfeiture adjustments. Cash-settled transactions are measured at fair value using Black-Scholes Merton and remeasured to fair value each reporting date. Treasury shares held by an Employee Benefit Trust are recognized at cost and deducted from equity, with no gain or loss, and used to settle share options. Foreign currency transactions are also addressed, though details are not given in the text.

nodes.title: Equity-settled Transactions:
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for equity-settled share-based payments, foreign currency transactions, derivative financial instruments and hedge accounting, and fair value measurement. Equity-settled payments are measured at fair value at grant date using Black-Scholes and Binomial models and charged appropriately. Foreign currency transactions are recognized at transaction date rates, with monetary items retranslated at period-end rates and exchange differences recognized in profit or loss, except for certain borrowings and qualifying cash flow hedges. Derivative financial instruments are initially and subsequently measured at fair value, with gains or losses in profit or loss unless designated as hedges. Hedge accounting for cash flow hedges is detailed, including documentation, effectiveness assessment, recognition of effective and ineffective portions, reclassification, and discontinuation. Fair value measurement of financial instruments at each balance sheet date is also covered.

nodes.title: Hedge Accounting:
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies in the notes to standalone financial statements for the year ended 31st March 2025. It addresses foreign currency translation, specifically that historical cost items in foreign currency are not re-translated and exchange differences on monetary items are recognized in profit or loss, with exceptions for foreign currency borrowings related to assets under construction and qualifying cash flow hedges. It details derivative financial instruments and hedge accounting, including initial recognition at fair value, subsequent re-measurement, gain or loss recognition, types of derivatives used (forward contracts, interest rate swaps, cross currency swaps), prohibition of speculative derivatives, cash flow hedge accounting designation, documentation, effectiveness assessment, recognition of effective and ineffective portions in OCI and profit or loss, reclassification, and discontinuation. It also covers fair value measurement, including definition, market assumptions, valuation techniques, fair value hierarchy (Levels 1, 2, 3), transfers between levels, and management's policies and procedures. Finally, it introduces financial instruments, defining a financial instrument and beginning discussion of financial assets.

nodes.title: Initial Recognition and Measurement
nodes.summary:
Initial Recognition and Measurement
All financial assets are recognised initially at fair value. However, in the case of financial assets not recorded at fair value through profit or loss, transaction costs that are attributable to the acquisition of the financial asset are added to the fair value. However, trade receivables that do not contain a significant financing component are measured at transaction price (net of variable consideration). Purchases or sales of financial assets that require delivery of assets within a time frame established by regulation or convention in the market place (regular way trades) are recognised on the trade date, i.e., the date that the Company commits to purchase or sell the asset.

nodes.title: Subsequent Measurement
nodes.summary: The text details subsequent measurement of financial assets under four categories: debt instruments at amortised cost, debt instruments at FVTOCI, debt instruments/derivatives/equity instruments/mutual funds at FVTPL, and equity instruments at FVTOCI. It explains criteria for amortised cost (business model to collect contractual cash flows and SPPI), measurement using effective interest rate, and impairment recognition. For FVTOCI debt, criteria include business model of collecting cash flows and selling, with fair value changes in OCI, interest and impairment in P&L, and recycling on derecognition. FVTPL is residual, with optional designation to avoid accounting mismatch, and fair value changes in P&L. Equity investments in subsidiaries, associates, and joint ventures are at cost; other equity investments at fair value, with held-for-trading at FVTPL and irrevocable FVTOCI election for non-trading, no recycling. Interest income from FVTPL is in other income.

nodes.title: Classification and Measurement of Financial Assets
nodes.summary: The page outlines the classification and measurement of financial assets under Ind AS 109. It covers debt instruments at amortised cost, detailing the business model and SPPI criteria, initial and subsequent measurement using the effective interest rate method, and impairment recognition. Debt instruments at FVTOCI are explained with criteria, fair value measurement, recognition of fair value movements in OCI, and interest income, impairment, and foreign exchange in profit or loss. Debt instruments at FVTPL are described as a residual category, with optional designation to reduce accounting mismatch, and fair value changes recognized in profit or loss. Equity instruments are discussed, including subsidiaries, associates, and joint ventures at cost, other equity investments at fair value, held-for-trading at FVTPL, and irrevocable FVTOCI election for non-trading equity with no recycling. The document is part of the standalone financial statements for the year ended 31st March 2025.

nodes.title: Equity Instruments:
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for financial instruments under Ind AS 109. It details classification and measurement of debt instruments at amortised cost, FVTOCI, and FVTPL, including criteria and subsequent measurement. Equity instruments are classified as FVTPL or FVTOCI, with subsidiaries/associates/JVs at cost. Impairment uses the simplified approach with expected credit losses. De-recognition principles for financial assets are explained. Classification of financial liabilities and equity instruments is described, including initial recognition, subsequent measurement of financial liabilities at FVTPL, and treatment of gains/losses.

nodes.title: Financial Instruments: Impairment, De-recognition, Classification, and Measurement
nodes.summary: The notes cover accounting for financial instruments. Equity instruments in FVTPL are measured at fair value with changes in profit or loss. Impairment of financial assets (excluding FVTPL) is assessed at each reporting period using Ind AS 109's simplified approach, with expected credit losses on trade receivables calculated via a provision matrix based on historical loss experience. De-recognition occurs when contractual cash flows expire or risks and rewards are substantially transferred; if control is retained, a retained interest and associated liability are recognized, and differences on de-recognition are recognized in profit or loss. Financial liabilities and equity instruments are classified as debt or equity based on contractual substance. Equity instruments are recognized at proceeds net of issue costs. Financial liabilities are initially recognized at fair value, net of transaction costs for loans, borrowings, and payables, and include trade payables, borrowings, financial guarantees, and derivatives. Subsequent measurement depends on classification, with FVTPL liabilities (held for trading, designated, or separated embedded derivatives not designated as hedges) measured at fair value with gains or losses in profit or loss.

nodes.title: Financial Liabilities at FVTPL:
nodes.summary: These notes to the standalone financial statements cover accounting policies for financial instruments and revenue recognition. For financial assets, they detail measurement of equity instruments at FVTPL, impairment using the simplified approach with expected credit losses via a provision matrix, and de-recognition principles including retained interests and gain/loss recognition. Financial liabilities and equity instruments are classified by substance; equity is recorded at proceeds net of costs. Financial liabilities include those at FVTPL (held for trading and designated), loans and borrowings at amortised cost using EIR, and financial guarantee contracts measured at the higher of loss allowance and amortised amount. De-recognition of liabilities and embedded derivatives accounting are explained. Offsetting rules are specified. Revenue recognition covers contracts with customers, recognizing revenue upon performance obligation satisfaction (typically at a point in time) and determining transaction price net of variable consideration and incentives.

nodes.title: Accounting Policies for Financial Liabilities and Embedded Derivatives
nodes.summary: The page outlines accounting policies for financial liabilities under Ind AS 109, covering initial FVTPL designation, loans and borrowings measured at amortised cost using the effective interest rate method with gains/losses recognised in profit or loss, and financial guarantee contracts recognised initially at fair value and subsequently at the higher of loss allowance or amortised amount. It details de-recognition of financial liabilities when obligations are discharged, cancelled or expired, with differences recognised in profit or loss. It also defines embedded derivatives, their re-assessment triggers, and accounting treatment: not separated for financial asset hosts under Ind AS 109, but separated and measured at fair value for other hosts when risks are not closely related and the host is not held for trading or designated at FVTPL, unless designated as effective hedging instruments.

nodes.title: Offsetting of Financial Instruments:
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies: offsetting financial instruments when a legal right and intent to settle net exist; revenue recognition from contracts with customers, including performance obligations, transaction price, variable consideration, significant financing component, dividend income, interest income using EIR, and claims accounted on acceptance basis; contract liability recognition for advance payments; and leases, including identification of leases, lessee accounting with right-of-use asset and lease liability initial and subsequent measurement.

nodes.title: Revenue Recognition, Contract Liability, and Lease Assessment Notes
nodes.summary: The page presents financial statement notes covering revenue recognition details, including variable consideration, significant financing component, dividend income, interest income using effective interest rate, and accounting for insurance and other claims. It defines contract liability recognition for payments received before performance obligations are satisfied, presented as advances from customers and recognized as revenue upon transfer of control. It also covers lease assessment at contract inception, determining whether a contract contains a lease based on right to control an identified asset, economic benefits, and right to direct use. The sections are labeled 1.21 Contract liability and 1.22 Leases, forming part of the standalone financial statements for the year ended 31st March 2025.

nodes.title: As a Lessee:
nodes.summary: The text details lessee accounting: recognition and initial measurement of right-of-use assets and lease liabilities, subsequent depreciation, impairment, and remeasurement; lease liability measurement at present value using implicit rate or incremental borrowing rate, including fixed, variable, residual value guarantee, and option payments; remeasurement triggers and adjustments. It covers exemptions for short-term and low-value leases, sale and leaseback accounting for rights retained and fair value considerations. Additionally, it defines borrowing costs, capitalisation of qualifying assets, and income offset, and explains trade receivables measured at amortised cost less loss allowance, including de-recognition for without-recourse factoring and non-de-recognition for with-recourse arrangements.

nodes.title: Lease Accounting Policies and Borrowing Costs Notes
key_items: Short-term Leases and Leases of Low-Value Assets:
nodes.summary: The page covers lease accounting policies, including lease liability measurement and remeasurement, short-term and low-value asset lease exemptions, and sale and leaseback treatment. It also details borrowing costs, covering components, capitalization criteria for qualifying assets, income from temporary investments, and recognition of other borrowing costs as expenses.

nodes.title: 1.24 Trade Receivable:
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for trade receivables, including amortised cost measurement and derecognition under without-recourse factoring versus recognition as financial liability for with-recourse arrangements. It details government grants and subsidies recognition criteria for expense-related, asset-related, capital investment, below-market loans, and non-monetary assets. Exceptional items are defined as significant income or expense requiring separate disclosure. Finally, it outlines current and deferred tax provisions, covering measurement, treatment of interest and penalties, recognition outside profit or loss, and deferred tax asset/liability recognition exceptions.

nodes.title: Notes on Government Grants, Exceptional Items, and Income Tax Accounting
nodes.summary: The page covers accounting policies: derecognition of trade receivables and recognition of related liabilities as short-term borrowings; government grants and subsidies recognition criteria for expense-related, asset-related, capital investment schemes, below-market loans, and non-monetary assets; exceptional items definition and disclosure rationale; current income tax measurement, treatment of interest and penalties, recognition outside profit or loss, and management evaluation of tax positions; and deferred tax using the liability method, including recognition of deferred tax liabilities and assets with exceptions for goodwill, initial recognition of certain transactions, and probability of future taxable profit.

nodes.title: Deferred Tax:
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies in notes to standalone financial statements. It details derecognition of trade receivables sold but retaining risks/rewards, recognizing proceeds as financial liability. Government grants and subsidies recognition for expense items, assets, capital investments, below-market loans, and non-monetary assets. Exceptional items disclosure criteria. Provision for current and deferred tax, including measurement, recognition exceptions, review of deferred tax assets, and offsetting. Provisions and contingent liabilities recognition, discounting, disclosure, remote claims, contingent assets, and warranty provisions. Earnings per share calculation for basic and diluted EPS, adjusting for bonus issues, rights issues, splits, and dilutive potential shares.

nodes.title: Deferred Tax, Provisions, Contingent Liabilities, Warranty and EPS Notes
nodes.summary: The text covers deferred tax asset recognition, review, and measurement, including offsetting and recognition outside profit or loss. It details provisions and contingent liabilities: recognition criteria, discounting, contingent liability disclosure, treatment of remote claims, and prohibition on contingent asset recognition. Warranty provisions are recognized at sale based on historical experience and revised annually. Earnings per share section explains basic EPS calculation with weighted-average shares adjusted for bonus issues, rights issues, splits, and reverse splits, and diluted EPS adjustments for dilutive potential equity shares.

nodes.title: Key Accounting Judgements, Estimates, and Assumptions in Financial Statements
key_items: 1.30 Significant Accounting Judgements, Estimates and Assumptions:
• Assessment of Impairment of Investments in Subsidiaries, Associates and Joint Ventures:
nodes.summary: The text outlines significant accounting judgements, estimates, and assumptions required for preparing financial statements under Ind AS, noting that estimates affect reported amounts and are reviewed ongoingly. It details three key areas: lease classification under Ind AS 116, including lease term assessment and discount rates; litigation and contingencies, where liabilities are provided when probable and estimable, involving estimation uncertainty; and impairment assessment of investments in subsidiaries, associates, and joint ventures, which requires estimating value in use through comparison with net worth, market price, and performance projections. The text emphasizes that actual outcomes may differ from estimates and that changes are recognized prospectively.

nodes.title: • Useful Lives of Property, Plant and Equipment and Intangible Assets:
nodes.summary: The text covers key accounting policies and estimates: useful lives of property, plant, equipment, and intangible assets, including periodic review and revision of unamortized amounts; measurement of defined benefit obligations using actuarial valuations with assumptions on discount rates, salary increases, and mortality; recognition and measurement of provisions and contingencies based on present obligation, probable outflow, and reliable estimate; fair value measurement of financial instruments using valuation techniques like DCF when quoted prices are unavailable, involving judgment on liquidity risk, credit risk, and volatility; share-based payments measured using Black-Scholes and Binomial models, requiring assumptions on expected life, volatility, and dividend yield; recognition of cash dividend liability when authorized and no longer at the Company's discretion; and recent accounting pronouncements, specifically Ind AS-117 Insurance Contracts, which had no impact on the financial statements.

nodes.title: Key Accounting Estimates and Judgments in Financial Statements
key_items: • Recognition and Measurement of Provisions and Contingencies:
• Fair Value Measurement of Financial Instruments:
nodes.summary: The page covers four key accounting areas: measurement of defined benefit obligations using actuarial valuations with assumptions on discount rates, salary increases, and mortality; recognition and measurement of provisions and contingencies based on present obligation, probable outflow, and reliable estimate; fair value measurement of financial instruments using valuation techniques like DCF with observable inputs and judgment on liquidity risk, credit risk, and volatility; and share-based payments measured using Black-Scholes and Binomial models, requiring assumptions on expected life, volatility, and dividend yield. All assumptions are reviewed at each reporting date.

nodes.title: 1.31 Cash Dividend to Equity Holders of the Company:
nodes.summary: This text covers two main sections: accounting policies and property, plant and equipment (PPE) details. The accounting policies include cash dividend recognition to equity holders, where a liability is recognized upon shareholder approval, and recent accounting pronouncements, specifically Ind AS-117 Insurance Contracts, which the Company determined had no impact. The PPE section provides a detailed breakdown of gross block, accumulated depreciation, and net block for various asset categories (e.g., freehold land, buildings, plant and equipment) for the years ended March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024. It includes reconciliations of opening balances, additions, deductions, and depreciation, along with capital work-in-progress (CWIP) movement and ageing schedules. Additionally, it lists projects in progress and temporarily suspended, with details on overdue projects and their expected completion timelines.

structure.title: B) Capital work-in progress, whose completion is overdue or has exceeded its cost compared to its original plan:
structure.summary: This text presents CWIP ageing schedules for standalone financial statements as at 31st March 2025 and 31st March 2024. For each year, it details amounts in capital work-in-progress by age buckets (less than 1 year to more than 3 years) for projects in progress and temporarily suspended, totaling ₹2,776.44 crore and ₹7,115.64 crore respectively. It also lists capital work-in-progress overdue or exceeding original cost, itemizing specific projects with amounts to be completed in 1-2 years and other periods, including a temporarily suspended project in 2024, with subtotals for each category.

structure.title: B) Capital work-in progress, whose completion is overdue or has exceeded its cost compared to its original plan:
structure.summary: The section covers capital work-in-progress overdue or exceeding cost compared to original plan, including CWIP ageing schedules for 2025 and 2024, specific overdue projects with completion timelines, and temporarily suspended projects. It also details immovable properties not held in the company's name, with reasons such as transfers in process or legal proceedings, and covers co-owned PPE, R&D capital expenditure, and pre-operative expenses. Additionally, it includes lease disclosures (right-of-use assets, liabilities, sale and leaseback), notes on intangible assets, investments, share capital, reserves, borrowings, provisions, revenue, expenses, tax, EPS, contingent liabilities, segment reporting, related party disclosures, share-based payments, financial instruments under Ind AS 107 and 113, fair value measurements, financial risk management, capital management, key ratios, statutory disclosures, and the Independent Auditor's Report.

nodes.title: Projects
nodes.summary: The text presents notes to standalone financial statements as of March 31, 2025. It includes two comparative CWIP ageing schedules (2025 and 2024) categorizing capital work-in-progress by age (less than 1 year to more than 3 years), with separate totals for projects in progress and temporarily suspended. It also lists specific projects whose completion is overdue or cost exceeded, showing amounts to be completed in various timeframes, and notes no temporarily suspended projects in 2025 but one in 2024. Additionally, it provides a table of immovable properties whose title deeds are not in the company's name, detailing description, gross carrying value, title deed holder, whether the holder is a promoter/director/relative/employee, and property holding period.

nodes.title: Reason for not being held in the name of the Company
nodes.summary: The text details immovable property title deeds not held in the company's name as of March 31, 2024, listing property descriptions, gross carrying values, title deed holders (e.g., Aditya Birla Nuvo Limited, Jayashree Textiles Limited), whether holders are promoters/directors/relatives/employees, holding periods, and reasons such as transfer in process, legal proceedings, or pending transfer due to amalgamation/arrangement/merger/demerger. It also covers PPE held on co-ownership with other companies (company's share), PPE including R&D capital expenditure, and pre-operative expenses pending allocation included in capital work-in-progress with detailed expense breakdowns. Additionally, it references leases.

nodes.title: I. AS A LESSEE
nodes.summary: This section provides lease-related disclosures, including right-of-use assets, lease liabilities, maturity profiles, and amounts recognized in profit and loss and cash flows, with lease terms and borrowing rates. It covers sale and leaseback arrangements and extensive notes on intangible assets, investments, share capital, reserves, borrowings, provisions, revenue, expenses, tax, EPS, contingent liabilities, commitments, segment reporting, related party disclosures, share-based payments, and financial instruments under Ind AS 107. Fair value measurements under Ind AS 113 include hierarchy, valuation techniques, Level 3 reconciliations, sensitivity analysis, and financial risk management objectives covering market risk (foreign exchange, interest rate, equity price), credit risk, and liquidity risk, with exposures, hedging, sensitivity analyses, and management strategies. Capital management objectives, debt-equity ratios, key ratios, and other statutory disclosures are presented. The Independent Auditor’s Report covers the audit opinion, key audit matters, responsibilities, CARO 2020 compliance, and internal financial controls.

nodes.title: I. AS A LESSEE (intro)
nodes.summary: The text presents lease-related disclosures from standalone financial statements: right-of-use assets' carrying value (gross block, accumulated depreciation, net block) for 2025 and 2024 with additions, deductions, and depreciation; lease deeds not executed in the Company's name, including property descriptions, title deed holders, carrying values, dates, and reasons; movement in lease liabilities (opening, additions, cancellations, finance cost, payments, closing); maturity profile of contractual undiscounted cash flows; lease liabilities in the statement of financial position (current/non-current); amounts recognized in profit and loss (interest, variable payments, short-term and low-value lease expenses); amounts in cash flows (total cash outflow); and lease terms (2–99 years) with weighted average incremental borrowing rates (5.17%–8.70%). Key totals and comparatives are included.

nodes.title: C. Sale and Leaseback
nodes.summary: This section covers sale and leaseback arrangements, including proceeds, equipment value, tenure, interest rates, and collections. It details movements in other intangible assets with ageing schedule, investments in subsidiaries, joint ventures, and associates with impairment testing, other non-current investments, non-current loans and assets, inventories, current investments, trade receivables, cash and cash equivalents, bank balances, current loans to related parties, and equity share capital details. It also covers shares kept in abeyance under Section 126, reconciliation of outstanding shares, rights issue, ESOP exercises, share capital suspense, rights and restrictions of equity shares, shareholding patterns, promoter group changes, reserves movements, other comprehensive income, borrowings, financial liabilities, provisions, deferred tax, revenue, expenses, exceptional items, tax, EPS, contingent liabilities, commitments, segment reporting, related party disclosures, share-based payments, and financial instruments under Ind AS 107.

nodes.title: C. Sale and Leaseback (intro)
nodes.summary: The text covers notes to standalone financial statements: sale and leaseback arrangements with proceeds, equipment value, tenure, interest rates, and collections; detailed movement of other intangible assets (gross block, accumulated amortization, net block) for FY25 and FY24, including intangible assets under development with ageing schedule; investments in subsidiaries, joint ventures, and associates (quoted and unquoted) with ownership percentages, impairment testing using DCF, and key assumptions; other non-current investments (quoted and unquoted) at fair value; non-current loans, other financial assets, and other non-current assets; inventories with provisioning; current investments in debentures, mutual funds, and certificates of deposit; trade receivables with ageing schedule and allowance; cash and cash equivalents; bank balances; current loans and advances to related parties with terms; other current financial and non-current assets; and equity share capital including authorised, issued, subscribed, and paid-up details, rights issue, and share capital suspense.

nodes.title: Shares kept in Abeyance
nodes.summary: This section covers equity share abeyance under Section 126, reconciliation of outstanding shares including rights issue, ESOP exercises, and share capital suspense. It details rights, preferences, and restrictions of equity shares, rights issue terms, shareholding patterns, promoter group changes, and shares reserved for ESOPs. Notes to standalone financial statements detail movements in securities premium, treasury shares, ESOP reserve, general reserve, and retained earnings. Other comprehensive income components, nature of reserves, borrowings, financial liabilities, provisions, deferred tax, revenue, expenses, exceptional items, tax, EPS, contingent liabilities, commitments, segment reporting, related party disclosures, share-based payments under various ESOS schemes, and financial instruments under Ind AS 107 are also covered.

nodes.title: Shares kept in Abeyance (intro)
nodes.summary: The text covers equity share abeyance under Section 126 (61,985 fully paid shares and 3,025 rights shares), reconciliation of outstanding shares including rights issue partly paid shares converted, ESOP exercises, and share capital suspense. It details rights, preferences, and restrictions of equity shares (dividend, voting, liquidation), the rights issue terms and proceeds usage, confirms no holding company, lists shareholders holding over 5% and promoter group shareholding with changes (including BGHPL increase via amalgamation), shares reserved for ESOPs, and other equity components (capital reserve, securities premium, treasury shares, ESOP reserve, general reserve, retained earnings, and other comprehensive income).

nodes.title: Standalone Financial Statement Notes on Reserves and Equity
nodes.summary: This page presents notes to the standalone financial statements for the year ended 31st March 2025, detailing movements in five equity components. Securities Premium section tracks opening balance, ESOP exercises, transfers from Employee Stock Option Reserve, rights issue proceeds, call in arrears, share issue expenses, and closing balance. Treasury Shares shows opening balance, purchases, issues, and closing balance. Employee Stock Option Reserve covers opening balance, options granted net of lapses, loss on treasury shares issued, transfer to Securities Premium, cancellation of vested options, and closing balance. General Reserve includes opening balance, cancellation of vested options, and closing balance. Retained Earnings details opening balance, profit for the year, FVTOCI gain/loss on equity sale, defined benefit remeasurement gain/loss net of tax, dividends paid, and closing balance.

nodes.title: g) Other Comprehensive Income
nodes.summary: The section covers notes to Grasim Industries' standalone financial statements for FY2025, including Other Comprehensive Income components, nature of reserves, borrowings, financial liabilities, provisions, deferred tax, revenue, expenses, exceptional items, tax expense, EPS, and contingent liabilities. It details contingent liabilities across tax and regulatory domains with amounts, capital and financial commitments, segment reporting, and related party disclosures. It also covers share-based payments under ESOS-2013, ESOS-2018, and ESOS-2022, including grant details, valuation assumptions, movement of options, and expenses recognized. nodes.title: g) Other Comprehensive Income (intro)

It outlines criteria for Significant Increase in Credit Risk, including account deterioration, comprehensive risk factor assessment for large borrowers, use of credit ratings, and adverse news. Finally, it describes the grouping of financial assets for Expected Credit Loss (ECL) calculation: individual assessment for corporate portfolios and collective assessment for retail portfolios and homogeneous pools based on common characteristics.

4. Credit Risk:
Credit risk arises when a customer or counterparty does not meet its obligations under a customer contract or financial instrument, leading to a financial loss. The Group is exposed to credit risk from its operating activities primarily trade receivables and from its financing/investing activities, including deposits with banks, mutual fund investments, and investments in debt securities, foreign exchange transactions. The Group has no significant concentration of credit risk with any counterparty.
The carrying amount of financial assets represents the maximum credit risk exposure.
